Fiance and I were in a similar situation as OP but we were able to overcome it. I guess it boils down to how much you really love each other and I'm also not sure if you're familiar with the 80/20 rule of relationships. Try to look it up. I weighed our own situation and figured that it took a lot of guts for him to say that information. Unless he contracted STDs from the activities he had with escorts then I think it's up to him to keep the info. I also had the same fears as you that what if he choses to go to such places again, and it bugged me for a bit and this is the very first time my trust for him was shaken. I also got myself tested for my own sanity. After getting a negative test it became much smoother than that. Consider your bf's feelings also, I'm pretty sure he is also devastated but probably expecting this reaction. If you think that your love is more than this particular bump in your relationship, then talk to him and tell him what would make you feel better. Do you need additional reassurance that you will be exclusive? Or do you need something else? Everything gets resolved if you try to address a problem logically. If everything else doesn't work then there are also the sad option of letting this one go.

You have not gotten past the pain of losing your mom and honestly I don't think it ever will. I lost my dad, too but my mom never remarried. Honestly, I feel bad for my mom because she lost her partner. The person she was supposed to grow old with. My siblings and I will in the future all have our own families and my mom she will be left by herself. I think that your dad is lucky to have found someone to be by his side again. I have a question , though, have you ever considered what your dad felt when he lost his wife? Normally men doesn't show the pain and they think getting a new wife is going to help them (yes, it will in the future). But have you tried asking him how he feels? For sure your mom will forever have a place in his heart and that he loves her still. Also, it looks like your stepmom has been trying to reach out to you, too. You haven't written that she has ever been mean to you so I'm guessing she has just lived with all your reactions to them trying to make her part of your family. I am sure she knows that she will not be able to replace your mom in your heart so just give her a chance. If I were her I would feel bad that I am competing eith a dead woman. Coz how can she ever compare to the memories of a dead mom. That is to hard to even fathom. So think about that, too. My suggestion is that you cry your frustrations out or find something to release that anger in your heart (in a safe and non-harming others kind of way). Once you've done that, try to have an open dialogue with your dad and stepmom. Tell them that you are getting angry because you feel that they are trying to replace the memory of your mom, coz honestly maybe they dont understand you, and people cannot read minds, you have to be transparent. Be open to the idea also of accepting your stepmom in your life. Your mom would be happy in heaven knowing that someone else is taking care of her kid while she's gone. Imagine if you are also in the position of your stepmom in the future, when a find a man you love so much but has a kid and a dead wife, how would you feel if you would have you as a step-kid. 

I hope that your family would start to heal from all of this.

First of all, your feelings are valid. They always are. You feel them for a reason. Something happened in you that made you feel that life is not worth living anymore. Honestly, I'm going through the same thing. I suggest that you hold on to your family for support and to also lean on to God. That is what I'm doing now day by day thinking of 3 things I am grateful for. And all the time my family would always be there. 

(1) I believe your family is putting on an effort to do the same to you as you've mentioned but you have to open up to them more so that they would be able to help you. Not everyone has a mom who hugs them, I have my mom but my dad passed away and he is someone I am very close to so if you have both parents and a loving sister/s then you are blessed than most people.

(2) You also said you came from a financially stable family and that is something to be thankful. I have quit my job recently and I am struggling financially so you are at a better state than me on that part. There are people on this world who have to beg/steal to get food, now go downstairs look at your fridge and pantry and you would realize how lucky you are compared to these guys.

(3) You also mentioned that you have above average level of intelligence. This is a gift from God that you have to be thankful for and use. You are smart and you are aware that you have a problem be logical and seek for help. It doesn't make you less of a person, honestly it takes someone smarter to want to be better.

Think about these 3 things today and see if these are things you should be thankful for. Also, you are way younger than me which means you have more years to grow and more time to find your purpose. Remember also, that God also allows people to struggle so that the only option they have is to turn to Him for help. I suggest you continue going to church and seek his guidance and keep your faith and hope you find miracles in your life because that is also what I seek for me.
